root.name: King's Indian Attack: French Variation
root.moves: 1. Nf3 d5 2. g3 c5 3. Bg2 Nc6

overview: White plays the King's Indian Attack set-up of Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, d3, Nbd2 and e4, while Black meets it with a Sicilian-style ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...e6 and later ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O. White aims at e4 and a kingside attack with Re1, e5 and Nf1-g3 or h4, and Black hits back on the queenside and in the centre. The game is manoeuvring with a clear plan for each side.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto, castle, d3, Nbd2 and e4, then e5 and a kingside attack.
Play for h4-h5 and Ng5 or Nf1-e3 pressure on the king.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...e6, ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O, then queenside play with ...b5 and ...Rb8.
Strike in the centre with ...d4 or ...dxe4 when White commits.

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d3, e4, g3 against Black's ...c5, ...d5, ...e6; reversed-Sicilian/French feel.

character.notes: Plenty of room for slow play with clear plans; moderate risk on both sides.

structure.notes: Centre not locked; tension on d5/e4, flank openings are Flexible.

approach.notes: KIA is a system White plays against almost anything.

level.notes: Clear plans and little to memorise; moderate subtlety against ...c5.

character.reason: Manoeuvring game with chances for both sides, neither forcing nor especially solid.

structure.reason: Flank-opening centre, tension on e4 and d5.

level.reason: Clear plans but real middlegame subtlety.

plans.reason: Typical KIA plan is e4 and a kingside attack with the g2 bishop.
